issues.title: Logger uses direct logging.getLogger initialization
issues.description: The rule requires logger instances to be created using the pattern `logger: "logging.Logger" = get_logger("module_name")` from prefect.logging, but the code uses the direct `logging.getLogger(__name__)` pattern instead.
issues.problematic_code_snippet:
# Logger for SDK fetcher operations
logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
issues.rule_name: Logger Instances Must Follow Standard Initialization Pattern

issues.title: Incorrect deployment filtering breaks full-name matching
issues.description: The deployment filtering logic checks `dep.name not in deployment_names` instead of checking `full_name not in deployment_names`. This causes the filter to incorrectly evaluate when users specify deployment names in 'flow-name/deployment-name' format. When a user provides a full deployment name like 'my-flow/production', the code checks if 'production' (the short name) is in the list containing 'my-flow/production', which fails, causing the deployment to enter the fallback matching logic unnecessarily. This breaks the fast-path check and could lead to incorrect filtering behavior where deployments are included or excluded inappropriately.
issues.problematic_code_snippet:
# If filtering by deployment name, check the full name matches
        full_name = f"{flow_name}/{dep.name}"
        if deployment_names and dep.name not in deployment_names:
            # Only include if the full name matches (filter was by name parts)
            # Skip if user specified full names and this doesn't match
            found_match = False

issues.title: Missing type validation for work pool job variables schema
issues.description: The code removes the `isinstance(variables, dict)` type check before assigning `base_job_template["variables"]` to `job_vars_schema`. The `job_vars_schema` variable is typed as `dict[str, Any]` and is expected to be a dictionary throughout the SDK generation process. If `base_job_template["variables"]` contains a non-dict value (like a list, string, or other type due to malformed work pool configuration), this will cause type inconsistencies that could lead to runtime errors in downstream code that expects a dict, such as the template renderer or SDK generator that processes the schema.

issues.title: Removed strict zip validation enables silent data corruption
issues.description: The code removes `strict=True` from the `zip(pool_names_list, results)` call in the work pool parallel fetching logic. The strict parameter ensures that both iterables have the same length and raises a ValueError if they don't match. Without it, if there's a mismatch between the number of work pool names and the results from `asyncio.gather()` (which should never happen in correct code but could occur due to bugs in the async gather logic or unexpected exceptions), the zip will silently truncate to the shorter sequence. This means some work pool results could be dropped or mismatched with the wrong names, leading to incorrect work pool metadata in the generated SDK without any warning or error.

pr.author: unknown

structured_output.summary:
This PR adds two docs pages for the beta `prefect sdk generate` command (a how-to guide and a CLI reference page), wires them into `docs/docs.json`, and moves `form-building` into a new "Deployments" nav group. It also bundles four source edits into `src/prefect/_sdk/fetcher.py` that the title and description don't mention: a logger, a changed deployment-name filter, removal of a `zip(strict=True)`, and removal of a dict type guard.

The docs are mostly accurate. The CLI flags match `src/prefect/cli/sdk.py`, and the `with_options()` parameters match the template. The source changes are not safe to merge. The deployment-name filter change breaks short-name ambiguity detection, and the existing test `test_fetch_sdk_data_ambiguous_short_name_warning` fails at head (1 failed, 33 passed in `tests/_sdk/test_fetcher.py`). Ruff also reports four errors in `fetcher.py`, and the async example in the guide awaits a synchronous method.
structured_output.verdictRationale: A required test fails on the head commit because of the `dep.name not in deployment_names` change, which silently drops the ambiguous short-name warning. The change is also unrelated to the docs title and undocumented. Lint fails on the logger placed between imports, and a documented async example would raise TypeError at runtime. The docs themselves are close to correct, so the fixes are small.

architecture.overview:
`prefect sdk generate` is a Typer command in `src/prefect/cli/sdk.py`. It calls `generate_sdk` in `src/prefect/_sdk/generator.py`, which calls `fetch_sdk_data` in `src/prefect/_sdk/fetcher.py`. The fetcher checks authentication, pulls deployments, flows and work pools from the Prefect API with filters, and builds an `SDKData` model. The renderer then fills `src/prefect/_sdk/templates/sdk.py.jinja` to write a typed Python module with `deployments.from_name()`, `run()`, `with_options()` and `with_infra()`.

This PR does not change the pipeline's shape. It adds two MDX pages and nav entries under `docs/`, plus small edits inside the fetcher. The fetcher edits change how `--deployment` filters are matched and how the logger is set up. The filter change is the one that alters runtime behavior.
steps: Entry point: the user runs `prefect sdk generate --output`, with optional `--flow` and `--deployment` filters. `src/prefect/cli/sdk.py` parses these and calls `generate_sdk`.

Fetch: `fetch_sdk_data` in `src/prefect/_sdk/fetcher.py` checks authentication and builds server-side flow and deployment name filters. It then fetches deployments, flow names and work pools in parallel.

Filter (changed by this PR): line 397 now skips the client-side check for any deployment whose bare name is in the filter list. That skips the path that records short-name matches for the ambiguity warning. Full `flow/deployment` names still match through the later loop.
Render: `SDKData` is passed to the renderer and `templates/sdk.py.jinja`, which emits the typed module. The `with_options` and `with_infra` parameters the docs list are defined there.

Docs (added): `docs/v3/advanced/generate-custom-sdk.mdx` is a how-to guide. `docs/v3/api-ref/cli/sdk.mdx` is the CLI reference. `docs/docs.json` registers both, and `form-building` moves into a new Deployments group under Advanced.

findings.title: Short-name deployment filter no longer records ambiguity warnings
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/prefect/_sdk/fetcher.py`, line 397 in `fetch_sdk_data` was changed from `if deployment_names and full_name not in deployment_names:` to `if deployment_names and dep.name not in deployment_names:`. Revert that condition to `full_name not in deployment_names`. The short-name ambiguity tracking below it depends on that block running for bare names. Then run `pytest tests/_sdk/test_fetcher.py`. `test_fetch_sdk_data_ambiguous_short_name_warning` should pass, and the full-name filter tests should still pass.

findings.title: Guide awaits a synchronous `future.result()`
findings.fixPrompt: In `docs/v3/advanced/generate-custom-sdk.mdx`, the async example around line 132 has `result = await future.result()`. `PrefectFlowRunFuture.result` in `src/prefect/futures.py` is synchronous. Change the example so it doesn't await it. Either use `result = future.result()`, or call `await future.wait_async()` first and then read the result synchronously. Keep the rest of the example, and keep the existing `asyncio.run(...)` call at the bottom unchanged.

findings.title: Logger inserted between imports breaks lint
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/prefect/_sdk/fetcher.py`, the module-level `logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)` (around line 19-20) sits between `import prefect` and `from prefect._sdk.models import (...)`. Move it below the last import in the module, after `from prefect.settings.context import get_current_settings` and the `TYPE_CHECKING` block. Then run `ruff check src/prefect/_sdk/fetcher.py` to confirm E402 and I001 are gone.

findings.title: Unexplained removal of `zip(strict=True)`
findings.body:
`_fetch_work_pools_parallel` used `zip(pool_names_list, results, strict=True)`. This PR drops `strict=True`. Both lists are built from the same sorted names, so lengths always match and the guard never trips today. Removing it only removes a safety check that would catch a future mismatch. `requires-python` is `>=3.10`, so the removal isn't needed for compatibility either.

::diff{file="src/prefect/_sdk/fetcher.py" lines="218-221"}
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/prefect/_sdk/fetcher.py`, `_fetch_work_pools_parallel` (around line 220) changed `zip(pool_names_list, results, strict=True)` to `zip(pool_names_list, results)`. Restore `strict=True`. The project targets Python 3.10+, where `zip(strict=True)` is available. This matches the base revision.

findings.title: Unrelated removal of dict type guard in `_fetch_work_pool`
findings.body:
The `isinstance(variables, dict)` check was removed. `job_vars_schema` is annotated `dict[str, Any]`, so the check guarded against a non-dict `variables` value. Now a non-dict value is passed through unchecked into `WorkPoolInfo.job_variables_schema`. This is a behavior change that isn't in the PR title or description and has no test.

::diff{file="src/prefect/_sdk/fetcher.py" lines="179-183"}
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/prefect/_sdk/fetcher.py`, `_fetch_work_pool` (around lines 179-183) dropped the `isinstance(variables, dict)` guard before assigning `job_vars_schema`. Restore the guard so that only dict values are used, or else explain in the PR why it's safe to drop. Keep the `job_vars_schema: dict[str, Any] = {}` default.

findings.title: Nav and CLI reference structure is consistent
Guide's `with_options`/`with_infra` parameters match the template
findings.body: I checked the parameters the guide lists for `with_options()` (`tags`, `idempotency_key`, `work_queue_name`, `as_subflow`, `scheduled_time`, `flow_run_name`) against `src/prefect/_sdk/templates/sdk.py.jinja` (around lines 85-115), and they match. The `run()` return type `PrefectFlowRunFuture` also matches the guide's description. The only broken example is the async one flagged above.
